Renting with Friends: Legal Pitfalls of Co-Signing a Lease

Author: Anushka Sil

Co-signing a lease with your college roommates could legally make you responsible for their entire share of the rent — not just your own.
Shared housing is more common than ever among students and young professionals in India, but most roommates never realise that a co-signed lease creates joint liability for every tenant on it, not just individual responsibility.

By Anushka Sil, this article covers:
🏠 What "joint and several liability" actually means when multiple tenants co-sign one lease 
💰 The most common legal pitfalls — from unpaid rent to property damage to security deposit disputes 
📄 Why a roommate agreement is legally separate from your lease, and why you need both 
✍️ The essential clauses every roommate agreement should include, from rent-sharing to an early-exit plan

For anyone splitting rent with friends or colleagues, this is the legal safety net most people skip until it's too late.

comment: An often missed issue is exit planning—when one roommate leaves, the remaining tenants may inherit the financial burden unless the lease, replacement process, and indemnity terms are clearly addressed.
